To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we used state-of-the-art proteomics methods to identify the phosphorylation profile of ARCaP cells and to identify key pathways and proteins that contribute to the aberrant responses of this cell line to androgen.

we identified 385 phosphorylated proteins from androgen-repressed prostate cancer cells by using a combination of three enrichment strategies and that we identified APRIN as a potential androgen-repressed protein that may contribute to ARCaP cell growth and metastasis.
we have identified 385 phosphopeptides and 385 phosphoprotein in ARCaP cell line.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a robust and sensitive method for phosphoproteome profiling and the identification of potential novel phosphorylation-dependent signaling pathways in androgen-repressive prostate cancer cells.
the identification of phosphorylation sites in ARCaP cell lines, which are highly metastatic and androgen independent.

the development of a novel strategy for the enrichment of phosphorylated peptides from complex biological samples, the application of this method to the analysis of the phosphoprotein profiles in androgen-repressible prostate cancer cells, and the identification of potential novel biomarkers for prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CPP-TiO(2) coupled with FT-ICR mass analysis is an excellent approach to identify and characterize phosphopeptides in complex biological samples.
CPP coupled with TiO(2 )is the method of choice for the analysis of phosphoproteomes.

the phosphoproteomic profile of ARCaP cells has been characterized and the identified proteins and their phosphorylation sites have provided new insights into the mechanisms underlying ARCaP growth and progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the calcium phosphate/TiO(2) method is the best approach to identify phosphorylated proteins in human prostate cancer cell lines and that phosphorylated APRIN is involved in the aberrant responses of ARCaP cells to androgen deprivation.
we have identified 385 phosphopeptides and 385 phosphoprotein species from ARCaP, a highly metastatic androgen-repressed cell line, by combining CPP with the TiO2 method.
the combination of CPP/TiO(2) with the LTQ/FTICR mass spectrometry is a powerful strategy for phosphoproteome characterization.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of calcium phosphate precipitation and TiO( 2)-modified metal affinity chromatography coupled with Fourier transform ion cycloton resonance mass spectrometric (FT-ICR-MS) analysis is a powerful strategy for phosphoproteomics.
mass spectrometry is a powerful tool for characterizing the phosphoproteomic profiles in androgen-repressive prostate cancer.

the phosphoproteomic profile of a human prostate cancer cell line can be comprehensively characterized by the use of a hybrid mass spectrometer with a high resolution FTICR mass analyzer, and that the calcium phosphate precipitation/TiO(2) strategy is the most sensitive, efficient, and specific method to enrich phosphopeptides from complex biological samples.
